text: Theo builds the FinOps dashboard Lesson 1's mandate asked for, following the Inform stage of the FinOps framework: one screen where Casey and Dana can answer, in plain terms, are we spending what we expected, and do we have the capacity we think we have. Four panels: daily spend by cloud, cost per namespace, cluster-wide utilization, and budget burn-down.

Cost data comes from Azure Cost Management, queried in KQL by resource group. Capacity data comes from Container Insights, averaged across every node in the apppool node pool. Both live in the same Grafana dashboard, on the same timeline — a cost conversation and a capacity conversation, using the same numbers.

That cluster-wide average answers a real, specific question: across all the compute Driftwood is paying for, how much of it is being used in total. That's the standard, defensible figure for a FinOps dashboard, and nothing about building it this way is a mistake.

But an average answers how much, not how evenly distributed. Twelve nodes at 20 percent and three nodes pinned at 95 percent can still average out to something healthy-looking. That's a different question than whether anything is actually struggling right now — a reliability question, for a different dashboard, that this capstone's incident runs straight through later on.
